A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of TokenSkip, with matching authors, methods, and main experiments. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original TokenSkip experiments on GSM8K, MATH-500, and MMLU-STEM, together with compression analyses and CoT recovery examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds CommonsenseQA experiments in Appendix C.2 and Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same importance-based token pruning, mixed-ratio fine-tuning, and ratio-conditioned autoregressive inference. The CommonsenseQA experiment applies the existing method without introducing a new component or procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds CommonsenseQA training and validation experiments, extending the existing math/STEM coverage to commonsense multiple-choice question answering. GSM8K, MATH-500, MMLU-STEM, and the existing transfer scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BeConcise, OnlyNumbers, AbbreWords, LC-Prompt, and Truncation; Figure 8 retains the same importance-metric comparisons. The new CommonsenseQA table uses the original-model comparator already used in the Qwen experiments, introducing no new comparison method.

E3.justification: The new CommonsenseQA experiment uses 9,700 training samples and evaluates on the validation set, reporting Qwen2.5-7B/14B results at ratios from 0.5 to 1.0. This adds an experimental setup; previously stated splits, metrics, budgets, and testing procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The compression-ratio, token-importance, length-budget, recovery, and case-study analyses are retained. The existing out-of-domain evaluation moves from B.4 to C.1 without substantive changes. CommonsenseQA adds benchmark evaluation with task-specific training, rather than a new robustness or transfer analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the performance comparisons. Table 5 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds CommonsenseQA results while existing numerical results and plotted findings remain unchanged. At ratio 0.5, Qwen2.5-7B reports 80.6% accuracy and 128.43 tokens versus the original model's 80.3% and 272.13; Qwen2.5-14B reports 82.1% and 121.03 versus 82.1% and 247.81. These are new benchmark results, not improvements over v2 under an existing setting.

T1.justification: The token-importance definitions, pruning equations, training objective, and inference formulation are unchanged. No assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty, controllability, and efficiency claims. The new benchmark supplies additional support without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix C.2 explicitly extend the applicability discussion to reasoning beyond mathematics, interpreting CommonsenseQA results as evidence of roughly 50% CoT reduction without accuracy degradation. Existing mechanism explanations and stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 retains the same LoRA settings, optimizer, training schedule, software, hardware, and decoding details; code and checkpoint access information is unchanged. The new experiment adds sample-count and split information under E3, without additional implementation or access instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds the CommonsenseQA citation to Talmor et al. (2019) and its reference entry. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier compression and efficient-reasoning methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: B.4 becomes C.1 within a new Additional Experiments appendix, followed by C.2. v3 also adds acknowledgements and updates the Section 4.2 appendix reference. The main narrative otherwise remains substantially identical.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 5 and moves Table 4 upward on the final appendix page to accommodate it. Acknowledgements reflow the references, and printed page numbers disappear. Existing figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.2 and Table 5 strengthen empirical support beyond the earlier math/STEM coverage: the 14B CommonsenseQA experiment reports unchanged 82.1% accuracy while average tokens fall from 247.81 to 121.03. This is a useful, limited extension of task applicability. Because it uses CommonsenseQA training data, it does not establish transfer from math training to commonsense reasoning. The existing method, results, and analyses remain intact.
